REUTERS: Mexico 'pragmatic' on USMCA talks, Canada still offers no concessions, Greer says
July 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 US Trade Rep Jamieson Greer, at the Aspen forum: "It's going well with the Mexicans. They're quite pragmatic." In trade-talk, "pragmatic" means moving toward Washington's terms — with Canada cast as the holdout. 🔍

Greer names the actual goal: "our trade deficit with Mexico really is a challenge... a problem," adding he'd rather US firms buy from Mexico than China. Mexican cooperation becomes the baseline; any pushback becomes the deviation.

• Greer: "It's going well with the Mexicans. They're quite pragmatic"
• Greer: the US "trade deficit with Mexico really is a challenge. It really is a problem"

REUTERS/AJ: Sheinbaum rejects DEA claim that Mexico's government is linked to cartels
July 15, 2026 | 🔴

📰 DEA Administrator Terry Cole called Mexico's government and the cartels "one and the same." The reporting notes no evidence was offered. Sheinbaum: it reads "more like a political statement than one backed by evidence." 💀

Cole heads the agency policing the country that is, in Sheinbaum's words, "the world's largest market for illicit drugs" — the demand side the "deadly connection" framing keeps entirely on Mexico's side of the border.

• Cole: the government and cartels are "one and the same"
• Sheinbaum: the DEA "should focus on combating drug trafficking, distribution and money laundering within its own country"

PEW RESEARCH: Mexicans view Sheinbaum favorably, but less so than in 2025
July 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Pew leads with the decline. The number underneath the headline: 64% of Mexicans still view Sheinbaum favorably, 61% approve on the economy, 65% on education, 55% on US relations. 🇲🇽

The drop from 2025's 83% is real and reported straight — but "favorable, but less so" describes an approval rating most sitting leaders, Trump included, would take mid-term, in the middle of a US tariff war on their economy.

• favorable: 64% (down from 83% in 2025)
• approve on the economy: 61%; on education: 65%

AP: US designates 2 new Mexican cartels as foreign terrorist organizations
July 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 AP frames Washington adding the Juárez Cartel and Los Viagras to the terror list as "a further increase in pressure on President Claudia Sheinbaum" — eight Mexican groups now designated. Not one Mexican official is quoted. 🔍

The designation lets the US freeze assets and prosecute "material support," but AP leaves out both the US demand driving the trade and Mexico's standing objection that FTO labels build the legal groundwork for unilateral US action on Mexican soil.

• Rubio: the groups "threaten the security of US nationals... the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States"
• the sole quoted analyst discusses the designation's "strategic value for US border enforcement"

🇲🇽📊 MINIMUM WAGE NOW CLEARS THE BASIC BASKET — FOR THE FIRST TIME IN A GENERATION

A Mexican needed 4,888 pesos in June to cover the minimum basket of food and basic services, El Economista reports — and the cost actually fell 0.8% from May as inflation cools to a five-year low. Here's the shift: after the 4T more than doubled the minimum wage in real terms since 2018, a full month at minimum now clears that basket with room to spare. Through decades of neoliberalism, it didn't come close.

🇲🇽🩺 SONORA OPENS MEXICO'S FIRST HEALTH COORDINATION CENTER

Sonora just inaugurated Mexico's first Health Coordination Center (Cecosabi) — a C5-style command hub for public healthcare. From Hermosillo, 88 specialists monitor hospital bed availability in real time, dispatch ambulances, and coordinate emergency transfers across the state 24/7, on a 53-million-peso investment. Governor Alfonso Durazo says it will "optimize the coordination of all health services in the state," prioritizing the communities with the least medical coverage.

🔥🇲🇽 VERACRUZ WIPES OUT THE BOND DEBT OF ALL 199 MUNICIPALITIES

Veracruz just erased the bond debt of every one of its 199 municipalities — a neoliberal "bursatilización" scheme from 2008 that mortgaged towns' future federal transfers for quick cash. Municipalities had already paid 2,573 million pesos, 1,837 million of it pure interest. The state recovered 1,085 million from frozen trust funds and killed the debt 10 years ahead of its 2036 schedule. Governor Rocío Nahle: "We recovered the money. Today every municipality is settled — they don't have to pay a single peso."

🚨🇲🇽 DEA, FBI AND HSI RAN THE 'EL MAYO' RENDITION ON MEXICAN SOIL

New documents obtained by Contralínea show DEA, FBI and HSI agents ran the July 25, 2024 operation that grabbed "El Mayo" Zambada in Culiacán — an extraordinary rendition, not an arrest. The aircraft's tracking stayed dark until five minutes before landing; the FBI later paraded the same plane at an air show. Mexico's then-prosecutor Ernestina Godoy called it "a series of violations of Mexican and international law," and Sheinbaum said "everything indicates the US ambassador lied."

🚨🇲🇽 TRUMP REVIVES ICE TRAFFIC STOPS IN 24 HOURS — MEXICO FILES 17 CRIMINAL COMPLAINTS

Trump revoked the pause on ICE traffic stops within 24 hours — the same tactic tied to the deaths of Mexican nationals in US custody, which he called one of ICE's "most effective tools." Mexico isn't waiting: Sheinbaum's government has now formalized 17 criminal complaints with the US DOJ and state prosecutors over 17 Mexicans who died in ICE operations or detention. The latest, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo — 52, a construction worker, 35 years in the US, three US-citizen children — was shot by an agent in Houston on July 7.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO BACKS PANAMA CANAL NEUTRALITY — A DIRECT ANSWER TO WASHINGTON

Sheinbaum just put Mexico behind Panama's permanent neutrality treaty for the Canal. After two hours with President José Raúl Mulino at Palacio Nacional, she framed the region as "a space for growth — as long as respect is maintained, there is dialogue, and national sovereignty is respected between nations." Mulino thanked Mexico for defending the Canal "as a neutral instrument of world commerce" — a pointed reply to Washington's talk of taking it back.
